answer.label: fine-tune bias
answer.justification: Only logit-level data is available, and every logit value matches fine-tune bias closely. Raw-score shift ÷ TV is 11.3 ×10⁵. That is the deciding value: fine-tune bias averages 10.4, and every other class falls between 2.3 and 3.9. KL is 0.080 and TV is 0.083, against 0.082 and 0.082 for fine-tune bias. Top-1 agreement is 0.926 (0.935 expected) and sequence agreement is 0.547 (0.583 ± 0.05 expected). The Token-DiFR gap of 0.243 fits 0.219 ± 0.095. Quantization is ruled out by the raw-score ratio (2.3) and by its higher top-1 agreement (0.951). Fine-tune backdoor is ruled out by its higher KL (0.15) and ratio (3.3). Both system-prompt classes have KL of 0.24 or more and top-1 agreement of 0.89 or less, so they do not fit. Without activation or text data, the call rests mainly on the distinctive raw-score shift.
